sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the piedmont of the Abruzzo region, from the Gran Sasso chain - Maiella massif border (west) to the Tremiti Is. (east), across the high Pescara R. (west) and lower Sangro R. (east) valleys; it belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. S-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the central-southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show scarce intermediate seismicity in this region, but for the 101 A.D. (Mw 6.3) S. Valentino in Abr. Cit. destructive earthquakes that has affected the western sector of this source (although its age poses uncertainties concerning its epicenter and true intestiy). However, the zone falls within one of the mesoseismal areas of the catastrophic 5-30 Dec 1456 (Mw 7.0 and 6.6, respectively) multiple earthquake, that has affected a large portion of southern Italy. Given (1) the exceptional extents of the damage area, (2) the presence of at least 2/3 sub-regions where effects were maximum, and (3) the puzzling distance among these sub-regions, as of today historical catalogs have concentrated these events in two main sub-events, their epicenters falling approximately along the axis of the southern Apennines. However, this multiple earthquake holds several complexities that have been thoroughly addressed only in recent years, concerning at least the elusive damage distribution and the historical sources that firmly document it â€“ a task only complicated by the old age of the latter ones. All the more challenging is to explain the possible tectonic mechanism that has caused such unusually broad, seemingly contemporaneous peak destruction in areas (and even tectonic provinces) remarkably far away from one another. For an in-depth description of the 1456 seismic crisis, studied here and elsewhere in this Database, the reader can refer to Guidoboni and Comastri (2005), and Fracassi and Valensise (2007), and rererences therein.
This Source is a long strike-slip, right-lateral fault system that is thought to run ca. E-W across the Apulian domain, that here outcrops just SW of this source in the Maiella Mt. (to the west) to the Vasto high region (to the east), and the Tremiti Is. (offshore, further to the east, and NNW of the Gargano promontory). Such E-W trending tectonic mechanism seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. Field evidence in the area is scarce in the western sector of this source, while subsurface data (including pattern of geochemical anomalies and Rn leakage: see Ciotoli et al., 2004) in the Vasto High, and the E-W reactivation of inherited faults (see Brozzetti et al., 2006) in the Tremiti Is., suggest the presence of a deep-seated (rooting at ca. 20 km), blind set of structures whose westernmost segment has been associated with one mainshock of the 1456 sequence. This latter structure lies at the passage (from both a depth and kinematics viewpoint) between the shallower, NW-SE trending, outer extensional axis of the Abruzzo Apennines (to the west) and the deeper, blind, E-W trending, strike-slip right-lateral fault system that affects the Adriatic foreland (to the east).
To the west, this Source borders the comparatively shallower, SW-dipping, NW-SE trending outer extensional axis of the Abruzzo Apennines.
The western segment of this Source has been associated with one sub-event of the 1456 sequence. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the regional sub-surface structures. The dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. The rake represents oblique, right-lateral strike slip, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
